s:
Which of the following are envisaged by the Right against Exploitation in the Constitution of India?
1. Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour
2. Abolition of untouchability
3. Protection of the interests of minorities
4. Prohibition of employment of children in factories and mines
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: The Right against Exploitation is Arts. 23 (traffic and forced labour) and 24 (no child below 14 in factories, mines). Untouchability (Art. 17) is under the Right to Equality and minorities are under Arts. 29-30, so 1 and 4 only.

s: Which one of the following is a fundamental right under the constitution of India and a human right as well
x: Art. 21A makes education for children aged 6-14 a Fundamental Right as well as a human right (UDHR Art. 26). Information is statutory, and housing and a right to die are not Fundamental Rights.

s: Which one of the following is a human right as well as a fundamental right under the Constitution of India?
x: Art. 21A makes education for children aged 6-14 a Fundamental Right as well as a human right. Information, work and housing are not Fundamental Rights.

s: The bonded labour (Abolition) Act, 1976 is related to
x: The Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976 was enacted under Article 23, which prohibits begar and forced labour. Art. 24 is child labour, Arts. 25 and 27 are religion.

x: When an offence under IPC sections 175, 178, 179, 180 or 228 is committed before it, the Commission is deemed a civil court (Sec. 13 PHRA) and may forward the case to a Magistrate.

s: ____ constitutes the right to get pollution-free water and air. It ensures the right to 'live' is not merely confined to physical existence, but it includes within its ambit right to live with human dignity.

Right to Live in a Healthy Environment

Most books and keys: Right to Health and Information. Strictly: Laxmikanth lists both the right to health and the right to information among rights read into Art. 21, so every option is in the court's definition (Laxmikanth 8th ed. Part 1 (src/polity/laxmikanth-indian-polity-01) p.148-149).
The expected answer is 'Right to Health and Information', on the view that information flows mainly from Art. 19(1)(a); food/livelihood, education and a healthy environment are classic Art. 21 readings.

s:
Which of the following statements are true for the Fundamental Right to Life and Personal Liberty as guaranteed under Article-21 of the Constitution of India?

I. The Right is available to citizens as well as aliens.

II. It covers protection against arbitrary executive and legislative action.

III. It includes the right to live with human dignity.

IV. It can be taken away according to the procedure established by law.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below
x: All four hold: Art. 21 extends to citizens and aliens; after Maneka Gandhi it guards against arbitrary executive and legislative action; it includes life with dignity; and it can be curtailed only by procedure established by law.

s: Fundamental Duties enshrined in the Constitution are in consonance with
x: The Fundamental Duties (Part IVA, 42nd Amendment 1976) are in consonance with the UDHR, whose Art. 29 says everyone has duties to the community. CEDAW, WIPO and WTO have no such link.

s:
Other than the Fundamental Rights, which of the following parts of the Constitution of India reflect/reflects the principles and provisions of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948)?
1. Preamble
2. Directive Principles of State Policy
3. Fundamental duties
Select the correct answer using the given code below:
x: The Preamble (justice, liberty, equality, dignity), the DPSPs (work, living wage, education, health) and the Fundamental Duties (UDHR Art. 29: duties to the community) all reflect the UDHR, so 1, 2 and 3.

s: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides for a decent standard of life and full enjoyment of leisure and social and cultural opportunities?
x: Article 43 (DPSP) asks the State to secure a living wage, a decent standard of life and full enjoyment of leisure and social and cultural opportunities. Art. 42 is humane conditions and maternity relief; Art. 39 livelihood and equal pay; Art. 40 panchayats.

s: Which of the following is not a Social Act?
x: MISA (1971, repealed 1977) was an internal-security (preventive detention) law, not a social Act. The Dowry, Protection of Civil Rights and Immoral Traffic Acts fight social evils.

s:
Which of the following statements/statements is/are correct in relation to the Human Rights Commissions in India?

I. The role to undertake functions relating to human rights in the Union Territory of Ladakh may be conferred upon a State Human Rights Commission by the Central Government.

II. Only 2 persons can be appointed as members of the National Human Rights Commission under the category of possessing knowledge or practical experience with respect to human rights.

III. The President can remove the Chairperson of the State Human Rights Commission on the ground of proved misbehaviour. However, the President has to seek the opinion of the Supreme Court in this matter.

IV. The National Human Rights Commission is not empowered to inquire into any matter after the expiry of two years from the date on which the act constituting violation of human rights is alleged to have been committed.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Only III); it is added as option 5.
Only III is correct: SHRC members are removed only by the President, and for proved misbehaviour only after a Supreme Court inquiry on the President's reference. I is wrong (UT functions cannot go to an SHRC for Delhi, J&K or Ladakh), II is wrong (three human-rights members since 2019), IV is wrong (time bar is one year). (Printed key: None.)
